svg.title: LDA derived from Bayes' rule in one dimension
svg.desc: Three panels over x. First, two prior-weighted Gaussian densities, class A with area 0.75 and class B with area 0.25. Second, the logs of those densities, which are the straight lines delta A and delta B, crossing at x 0.38. Third, the posterior probability of class A, a sigmoid equal to one half at x 0.38, shifted right of the equal-prior curve.
svg.text: LDA from Bayes' rule, step by step (toy classes, but with unequal priors q_A = 0.75, q_B = 0.25)
② log of them: straight lines
The dropped term −½x² is the same for every class, so it cancels in the normalisation. A larger prior gives a class a higher line δ_c, so the boundary
moves toward the rarer class: from x = 0 (equal priors) to x = 0.38 here, because log(q_A / q_B) = log 3 shifts δ_A − δ_B by 1.10.
